items.title: Chagas disease and Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS): the challenge of confronting historical gaps.
items.abstract: Although many people affected by Chagas disease (CD) live in large cities and state capitals, a vast contingent remains dispersed across rural and sparsely populated zones, in extensive inland areas, much of it within a corridor stretching from the northeastern semiarid region to the southern Pampas, passing through the Cerrado of Central Brazil, a region severely affected by the endemic. Outside this wide belt where vectorial transmission has been virtually interrupted, new cases continuously emerge from the sylvatic circulation of Trypanosoma cruzi in the Amazon region. In different Brazilian regions, many of affected persons face major difficulties in accessing adequate medical care. They move through poorly defined therapeutic itineraries, where even basic procedures such as serological testing, electrocardiograms, or echocardiograms are difficult to obtain. It is necessary to map the most vulnerable and priority areas, to incorporate CD into primary health care programs through health information systems, to expand access to electrocardiographic evaluation with telemedicine support, to ensure referral and counter-referral systems to cardiology and gastroenterology outpatient clinics, to facilitate access to echocardiography, and to provide high-complexity procedures. In conclusion, it is crucial to build care pathways based on the organisational principles of the Unified Health System (SUS): universality, decentralisation, equity, comprehensiveness, and hierarchisation, as well as popular participation through patient associations and health councils. Upholding these principles for people affected by CD - and other cardiomyopathies - is essential not only for survival but also for ensuring dignity and hope, especially in inland communities, where more vulnerable populations depend on primary health care as the only gateway to treatment. In this article, we propose a general framework for their medical care.
authors: Dilma do Socorro Moraes de Souza

items.title: Exercise-Mimetic Irisin Nanoplatforms Orchestrate Mitochondrial Integrity and Neuroinflammatory Modulation in Cerebral Ischemic-Reperfusion Injury.
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, constrained by the narrow therapeutic windows and limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability of neuroprotective agents. Mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) are recognized as central pathological drivers of ischemic injury. While exerciese-induced neuroprotection provides promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by difficulties in standardizing exercise regimens and adapting them for patients with mobility impairments. Here, we report a bioinspired nanoplatform that integrates an exercise-mimetic strategy with precision mitochondrial protection to promote neuronal repair. The nanoplatform integrates Angiopep-2-mediated BBB penetration and a phenylboronate-modified multifunctional architecture, enabling lesion-specific cargo release and efficient ROS scavenging within ischemic neurons. In a murine model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), Ang-PPPC@irisin markedly restored mitochondrial integrity and attenuated neuroinflammation through regulation of the UCP2 pathway and enhanced ROS clearance, leading to a significant reduction of cerebral infarct volume. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing revealed anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective transcriptional programs. Notably, this strategy extended the therapeutic window beyond 4.5 h limit of thrombolytic therapies, highlighting its clinical potential. Our findings establish an exercise-inspired therapeutic strategy that combines BBB-penetrating delivery with mitochondria precision medicine, offering a translatable strategy for advancing stroke rehabilitation and broadening the scope of exercise-based interventions.

items.title: Expression of Circulating MicroRNA before and after Abdominal Aneurysm Repair.
items.abstract: Numerous studies have identified various miRNAs involved in aortic aneurysm pathology. This study investigated circulating miRNAs before and after abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (open surgical repair [OSR] or endovascular aneurysm repair [EVAR]). In this prospective, non-randomized, two-arm study, all eligible patients who underwent elective surgery from 2019 to 2021 for infrarenal aortic aneurysms were enrolled. Preoperative, postoperative (day 3), and follow-up serum samples (3 and 12 months) were collected. Circulating miR-29b/29c, miR-155, and miR-15a were analyzed using RT-qPCR. A total of 39 patients (87.2% male) were enrolled (Group I: OSR, n = 17; Group II: EVAR, n = 22). There were no significant differences in the expression of circulating miR-155, miR-15a, miR-29b, or miR-29c between Groups I and II during follow-up. However, subgroup analysis showed significantly lower expression of miR-15a in EVAR patients without an endoleak compared to those with an endoleak, as well as in patients undergoing open repair in the early postoperative phase (day 3). Our study found no significant differences in the expression of miR-155, miR-15a, miR-29b, or miR-29c before and after aneurysm repair, regardless of the surgical approach. However, early postoperative expression of miR-15a was significantly lower in EVAR patients without an endoleak, suggesting a potential role for miR-15a in early aortic remodeling following EVAR.

items.title: CPR outcomes in adults with Fontan physiology: Survival rates and advance care directives.
items.abstract: Outcomes from cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in patients with Fontan physiology are largely unstudied, contributing to a knowledge gap that makes advance care planning challenging. The goal of our study was to describe outcomes for adult patients with Fontan physiology who received CPR. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult patients with Fontan physiology who had at least one outpatient visit to an adult congenital heart center between 2006 and 2021 and sustained resuscitation for in- or out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Peri-procedural cardiac arrest cases were excluded. Of 46 patients across 10 centers, 22 (47.8%) had a lateral tunnel Fontan. The median age at cardiac arrest was 31 years (interquartile range: 26, 39). There were 27 (58.7%) in-hospital arrests. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 54.3% (95% confidence interval 40.0-68.7%). Survival to hospital discharge occurred in 43.5% (29.2-57.8%), and 34.8% (21.0-48.6%) survived to 1 year after CPR. Less advanced New York Heart Association class and cardiac arrest due to ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation were associated with increased one-year survival (p=0.02 and 0.01, respectively). Only 32.6% of patients had documented advance care planning discussions. In our cohort of adults with Fontan physiology receiving CPR, over half regained spontaneous circulation; however, only 34.8% were alive 1-year post-arrest. Because fewer than one-third of patients had documented advance care planning prior to arrest, the study highlights the need for proactive counseling and individual goals-of-care discussions in patients with Fontan physiology.
items.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

items.title: Cardiac amyloidosis: contemporary diagnosis and management with illustrative cases of ATTR and AL subtypes.
items.abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is an increasingly recognized, treatable cause of heart failure. Prompt distinction between transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and light-chain cardiac amyloidosis (AL-CA) is critical because delayed AL diagnosis can be fatal. This narrative review examines epidemiology, mechanisms, multimodality imaging, diagnostic algorithms, and established and emerging therapies. Literature was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library searches and reference screening; the original search dates require author confirmation. Emphasis is placed on immediate serum free light-chain and serum/urine immunofixation testing, nonbiopsy ATTR diagnosis in eligible patients, and TTR sequencing after ATTR confirmation. Three clinical cases illustrate diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Earlier diagnosis, urgent exclusion of AL-CA, universal TTR genetic testing, and multisystem evaluation of hereditary ATTR are essential. Multidisciplinary, phenotype-guided care and validated treatment-response measures will be increasingly important as therapies expand.

items.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer.
items.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor-stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor-adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

items.title: Developing an Interdisciplinary Framework for Behavioral Data Collection to Advance Coupled Behavioral-Epidemic Models: Cross-Sectional Study in 6 European Countries.
items.abstract: Human behavior influences infectious disease spread and the effectiveness of public health interventions. However, behavioral dynamics are often simplified in policy-oriented epidemic models, largely owing to the scarcity of suitable empirical data. This study aimed to develop an interdisciplinary approach to collecting theory-grounded behavioral data on SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, capturing the complexity and temporal dynamics of preventive health behaviors while quantifying factors relevant to epidemic modeling. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of adults in France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom from March to July 2024, using age-, sex-, education-, and region-based quotas. Guided by both the capability, opportunity, motivation-behavior model and the requirements of epidemic modeling, we combined validated instruments with modeling-oriented measures in the questionnaire. We assessed temporal changes in retrospectively reported perceived COVID-19 severity and willingness to vaccinate across 5 time points, associations between vaccination willingness, uptake, and timeliness, and differences in behavioral indicators by vaccination status. To capture interactions relevant to both disease transmission and information exchange, we measured age-specific in-person and discussion contacts. Selected measurements then informed a coupled behavioral-epidemic model to illustrate how intention-behavior gaps and changing intention shape simulated vaccination dynamics. After data quality filtering, 22,228 survey responses were analyzed. Vaccination willingness correlated with uptake and timeliness, although the proportion of initially unwilling respondents who received ≥2 vaccine doses ranged from 5.7% (95% CI 3.2%-8.3%) to 17.9% (95% CI 12.8%-23.1%) across countries. Respondents with low willingness delayed vaccination by approximately 2 months compared to those with high willingness (low willingness: 5.3 months, 95% CI 5-5.8; high willingness: 3.2 months, 95% CI 3-3.4). Respondents retrospectively reported declining perceived COVID-19 severity and willingness to vaccinate over time. Behavioral differences between vaccinated and unvaccinated respondents extended across 96% of the analyzed indicators (Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, P <.001) and were largest in the motivation domain. Vaccinated respondents reported higher vaccine confidence and trust in health authorities and lower concerns about vaccine safety. Average daily discussion contacts mirrored age-specific patterns of in-person contacts, ranging from 1.4 (95% CI 1.2-1.6) to 2.9 (95% CI 2.5-3.2) among adults aged <60 years across countries, compared with 0.5 (95% CI 0.4-0.6) to 1.2 (95% CI 1-1.4) among those aged ≥60 years. In model simulations, incorporating the intention-behavior gap increased vaccination coverage, while allowing willingness to change over time slowed uptake and reduced final coverage. This interdisciplinary approach provides a practical route from behavioral theory to empirical measurements that inform states, transitions, vaccination and social contact processes in behavioral-epidemic models. By providing an empirical basis for representing behavioral heterogeneity and dynamics, this study reduces reliance on simplified behavioral assumptions, supporting the development of more realistic behavioral-epidemic models and effective response strategies.

items.title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemoradiotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy alone for locally advanced rectal cancer: meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) achieves variable pathological responses. Incorporating immune checkpoint inhibitors into nCRT (inCRT) is a promising intensification strategy, but its efficacy and impact on surgical safety remain poorly defined. This meta-analysis evaluated the oncological benefits and surgical risks of inCRT versus nCRT in both proficient and deficient mismatch repair LARC. A systematic search of the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library databases was conducted for randomized clinical trials (RCTs) published from inception up to February 2026. The primary outcomes were pathological complete response (pCR) and grade ≥ III severe adverse events (SAEs) according to the Clavien-Dindo complication grading system. Secondary outcomes included major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative complications. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated using random-effects or fixed-effects models. Seven RCTs including 1117 patients were identified. Five trials did not restrict enrolment based on mismatch repair or microsatellite instability status, whereas two trials exclusively enrolled patients with mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable tumours. Although inCRT significantly increased the rate of pCR (31.9% versus 19.3%; RR 1.70; 95% confidence interval (c.i.) 1.37 to 2.10; P < 0.001) and MPR (55.1% versus 40.3%; RR 1.38; 95% c.i. 1.20 to 1.59; P < 0.001) versus nCRT, it was associated with a significantly higher risk of SAEs (30.1% versus 26.8%; RR 1.24; 95% c.i. 1.03 to 1.49; P = 0.02) and overall postoperative complications (32.8% versus 25.6%; RR 1.27; 95% c.i. 1.02 to 1.58; P = 0.03). Subgroup analysis indicated that the pCR benefit was most pronounced in cohorts receiving short-course radiotherapy and consolidation immunotherapy. The addition of immunotherapy to neoadjuvant therapy for LARC markedly improves pathological response but increases high-grade toxicity and surgical morbidity. Although inCRT is a potent intensification strategy, stringent patient selection and regimen optimization are required before widespread adoption.

items.title: Osteosarcoma: epidemiology, risk factors, molecular basis, clinical features, diagnosis, and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents and remains difficult to treat when metastatic, recurrent, or refractory, with survival outcomes particularly unfavorable in advanced disease. Although multimodal chemotherapy and surgery have improved outcomes for localized disease, therapeutic progress has been limited by marked inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity and the lack of reliable predictive biomarkers. OS pathogenesis reflects interconnected genomic instability, epigenetic dysregulation, aberrant signaling, metabolic reprogramming, stem-like cellular states, and interactions with the bone and immune microenvironment. These processes promote tumor progression, metastatic dissemination, and treatment resistance while complicating biomarker development and patient stratification. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by phospholipid peroxidation, has emerged as a potential metabolic vulnerability within this broader biological framework. However, its therapeutic relevance in OS remains context-dependent and is supported predominantly by preclinical evidence, with further validation required in clinically representative models. This review summarizes the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical features, diagnosis, molecular pathogenesis, and current management of OS, and critically evaluates emerging strategies, including targeted therapy, immunotherapy, ferroptosis modulation, nanomedicine, and ncRNA-based approaches. Particular attention is given to the strength of mechanistic evidence, biological heterogeneity, model limitations, safety, and translational barriers. Integrating these dimensions may support biomarker-guided patient stratification and more rational development of future OS therapies.

items.title: Molecular reprogramming of natural killer cells: crosstalk between PI3K-AKT-mTOR, MAPK, NF-κB, and epigenetic regulation.
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are key effectors of innate immunity. They rapidly eliminate virus-infected, transformed, and stressed cells while maintaining immune homeostasis. However, persistent inflammatory stimulation, tumor-associated immunosuppression, and metabolic stress progressively reprogram NK-cell phenotype and function, which leads to impaired cytotoxicity, defective cytokine production, metabolic dysfunction, and immune exhaustion. This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying NK-cell reprogramming in chronic diseases. It focuses on activating and inhibitory receptors, intracellular signaling pathways, transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, metabolic remodeling, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and non-coding RNAs. This review discusses how these interconnected mechanisms contribute to chronic inflammation, immune evasion, tumor progression, and metabolic disorders, ultimately impairing NK-cell-mediated immune surveillance. Finally, we highlight current therapeutic strategies to restore NK-cell function, including cytokine-based modulation, immune checkpoint blockade, metabolic intervention, adoptive NK-cell therapy, and CAR-NK cell therapy, along with their translational potential. Collectively, this review provides an integrated overview of the molecular mechanisms governing NK-cell dysfunction and discusses emerging therapeutic approaches for improving NK-cell-based immunotherapy in chronic diseases.

items.title: Progressive cutaneous nocardiosis due to Nocardia brasiliensis: A case report.
items.abstract: Primary cutaneous nocardiosis has a nonspecific presentation and may be mistaken for common bacterial or deep fungal infections. We describe a 59-year-old man with untreated chronic hepatitis C whose HbA1c was in the diabetic range and who developed a painful purulent forearm lesion after minor trauma while cleaning an abandoned building. The patient was managed as an outpatient. The infection progressed despite initial debridement and a 10-day course of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate, requiring repeat surgical debridement. Culture findings raised suspicion of Nocardia, and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry identified Nocardia brasiliensis. Broth microdilution demonstrated susceptibility to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, amoxicillin-clavulanate, ceftriaxone, amikacin, and linezolid, but resistance to imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and clarithromycin. Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg every 12 h was prescribed for a planned three-month course. The patient reported clinical improvement approximately six weeks after treatment initiation. This case emphasizes appropriate sampling, species-level identification, isolate-specific susceptibility testing, and surgical source control in progressive cutaneous nocardiosis.

items.title: Comparative Analysis Reveals Distinct Host Extrachromosomal Circular DNA Profiles Across HBV Infection and HBV-Associated Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNAs (eccDNAs) range from small microDNAs and small polydispersed circular DNAs to megabase-scale extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA). Although ecDNA has been implicated in virus-associated cancers, how oncogenic viruses influence the broader host eccDNA landscape remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized eccDNA in primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) infected with wild-type hepatitis B virus (HBV) or an HBV mutant lacking the regulatory X protein (HBVΔX) and compared these profiles with those of the HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cell lines Hep3B and PLC/PRF/5. Using genome-wide sequencing, computational analyses, and targeted experimental validation, we applied a gene-centric framework to identify loci recurrently represented on eccDNA and prioritized candidates relevant to HBV-associated hepatocarcinogenesis. We observed a heterogeneous eccDNA landscape that included a subset of recurrent gene-associated loci detected during acute HBV infection and altered expression of selected candidates in HBV-HCC models. These findings establish a framework for integrating eccDNA profiles across acute infection and transformed cellular contexts. More broadly, they support further investigation of eccDNAs as potential molecular records of virus-associated genomic stress and as candidate contributors to HBV-associated disease progression.

items.title: Profile of Migrant People With Non-Medically Supervised Use of Pregabalin: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Pregabalin is a gabapentinoid drug used to treat neuropathic pain, epilepsy, and anxiety. Over recent years, prescriptions and non-medically supervised use of pregabalin have increased in several European countries, especially within the French-speaking regions. These increases have been reported in young migrants, particularly those from Maghreb. However, the available peer-reviewed literature is poor with respect to the main characteristics of migrant people with non-medically supervised use of pregabalin and their trajectory of use. This scoping review explored both indexed scientific databases and gray literature to better identify the profile of pregabalin users, including their geographical origin, context and motivations of use, sociodemographic and psychiatric features. A search of relevant articles was conducted in several scientific databases of peer-reviewed journals, complemented by gray literature retrieved from reference lists of peer-reviewed publications and interviews with professionals involved in migrant support and healthcare. Two main populations of migrants using non-medically supervised pregabalin were identified. The first and main group consists of people coming from Maghreb, primarily from Algeria. They are commonly young socially marginalized men, who use pregabalin to experience euphoria or to cope with psychological trauma. These individuals usually migrate for economic reasons, and they frequently seek to specifically migrate to French-speaking countries for linguistic or family reasons. Pregabalin initiation is generally reported in the country of origin and continues post-migration, in the context of precarious living situations or enrollment in criminal networks that provide an easier access to the drug, in exchange for engaging in different illicit activities. The second identified population with non-medically supervised use of pregabalin comes from Eastern Europe and consists of older male individuals, who usually report using pregabalin to enhance or replace opioid drugs. In this second group, migration is motivated by economic or political reasons, and/or for getting access to healthcare services for chronic viral infections, such as human immunodeficiency virus or hepatitis B or C virus. They do not specifically aim to migrate into a French-speaking country. The increase in non-medically supervised use of pregabalin observed among migrant people in many Western European countries seems to be mainly related to two distinct migrant populations, i.e., Maghreb, and Eastern European countries, respectively. Between the two categories of migrant people, motivations for pregabalin use, as well as migration trajectories, seem to be different, suggesting that prevention, harm reduction, and treatment strategies should be tailored to each group.

items.title: TIM-3 Combined With Pan-Immune-Inflammation Value for Predicting Acute Rejection Risk After Kidney Transplantation.
items.abstract: Acute rejection remains a major obstacle affecting long-term graft survival after kidney transplantation, and current non-invasive predictive tools are still limited. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of early postoperative urinary soluble T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3 (sTIM-3) and pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) for acute rejection after kidney transplantation, and to establish a predictive model combined with other independent risk factors for acute rejection after kidney transplantation. The clinical data of 320 patients who underwent kidney transplantation at Shulan (Hangzhou) Hospital from January 2022 to April 2025 were retrospectively collected. Serum sTIM-3, urinary sTIM-3, and peripheral blood routine were measured on postoperative day 7, and PIV was calculated. The patients were divided into a rejection group and a non-rejection group according to the occurrence of acute rejection confirmed by biopsy within 6 months after surgery. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to screen independent risk factors and construct a predictive model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate the performance in discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility of the model. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that donor-recipient age difference ≥25 years (odds ratio [OR] = 7.347, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.299-23.482, p p = 0.015), PIV (per 100, OR = 2.121, 95% CI: 1.221-3.685, p = 0.008), and urinary sTIM-3 (per 10-unit increase, OR = 1.808, 95% CI: 1.484-2.204, p p = 0.69, χ 2 = 5.59 in the training set and p = 0.45, χ 2 = 7.81 in the validation set). Decision curve analysis showed that the model had a positive net benefit within the threshold probability range of 10%-60%, commonly used in clinical practice. Postoperative urinary sTIM-3 and PIV are independent predictors of acute rejection after kidney transplantation. The predictive model incorporating the donor-recipient age difference and HLA mismatch number demonstrated good performance in discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, providing a non-invasive tool for early risk stratification of acute rejection after kidney transplantation.
items.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)

items.title: Global Altitude Patterns in the Burden of Major Digestive System Cancers: An Ecological Study of 185 Countries.
items.abstract: The association between high altitude and the burden of digestive system cancer remains controversial, often lacking rigorous control for specific risk factors. This study assesses the ecological association between altitude-quantified as population-weighted mean elevation (PWME)-and the global burden of five major digestive system cancers. Cross-sectional data from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022 were integrated with longitudinal trends from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 across 185 countries. The association between PWME and cancer burden was assessed using multivariable linear regression models adjusting for socioeconomic, environmental, and cancer-specific confounders, e.g., red meat and alcohol consumption, obesity, and the prevalence of diabetes, Helicobacter pylori , hepatitis B, and hepatitis C infections. Longitudinal trends from 1990 to 2021 were assessed using joinpoint regression, and average annual percent changes were compared between high- and low-PWME strata. In the fully adjusted GLOBOCAN 2022 models, PWME was inversely associated with the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) of colorectal cancer ( B = -0.4192 per 100 m, 95% CI: -0.6676 to -0.1709, p = 0.0011) and positively associated with the ASIR of esophageal cancer ( B = 0.1177 per 100 m, 95% CI: 0.0044 to 0.2311, p = 0.0418). These incidence-related associations were also observed in GBD 2021 and were retained in the registry quality-restricted sensitivity analysis. Mortality-related findings and associations for gastric, liver, and pancreatic cancers were less consistent across datasets and sensitivity analyses. In descriptive longitudinal analyses, average annual percent change comparisons suggested divergent temporal trajectories between high- and low-PWME groups across several cancer burden metrics. Higher PWME was inversely associated with colorectal cancer incidence and positively associated with esophageal cancer incidence at the country level. These ecological associations are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously because altitude may capture multiple environmental, socioeconomic, lifestyle, healthcare, and data quality factors.
items.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)

items.title: Genetic differences shape the metabolic fates of tumors.
items.abstract: Distinct genetic alterations program metabolism to support liver tumor growth or immune evasion.

items.title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer.
items.abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras -driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c -MYC -driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c -MYC -driven PLCs, Pten -deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten -deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8 + T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF) - α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

items.title: Resection of Hepatic Metastases from Adrenocortical Carcinoma as a Treatment Modality: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare and aggressive neoplasm, generally associated with a poor prognosis. The liver is the main site of metastasis, and it is linked to worse clinical outcomes. Although there are still no standardized recommendations, surgical management of metastasis may be associated with better disease control. We conducted a systematic review to assess the oncological benefit of surgical resection of liver metastases in patients with ACC. We searched through Medline and Scopus databases following PRISMA recommendations. Outcomes included overall survival and disease-free survival. Five studies were identified, totaling 122 patients. In selected patients, surgical resection of liver metastases may be associated with increased overall survival, with a 1-year increase of 78% and a 5-year increase of up to 51.3%. Regarding adjuvant therapies, the presence of liver metastasis in ACC is an important adverse prognostic factor, particularly due to the limited response to systemic therapies. Although there is no consensus on the best therapeutic approach, evidence suggests that surgery, especially when combined with early adjuvant therapy, may improve clinical outcomes. Resection of liver metastases in patients with ACC, combined with adjuvant therapies, appears to improve outcomes in selected cases.
items.journal: Revista do Colegio Brasileiro de Cirurgioes

items.title: Liver resection, transplantation, and local therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma: a Brazilian multidisciplinary consensus.
items.abstract: Curative treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma is limited to strategies that achieve complete tumor eradication, primarily liver resection, liver transplantation, and locoregional therapies. However, therapeutic decision-making is complex and must balance tumor burden, liver function, patient characteristics, and resource availability. To develop multidisciplinary, evidence-based recommendations for the use of surgical and locoregional therapies in hepatocellular carcinoma management. The Brazilian Society of Surgical Oncology coordinated this consensus in collaboration with 13 additional Brazilian medical societies. A scientific steering committee identified clinically relevant questions addressing indications, patient selection, technical considerations, and outcomes related to liver resection, liver transplantation, and locoregional therapies. A total of 36 clinical questions reached consensus, generating evidence-based recommendations across three major domains: liver resection, including criteria for resectability, assessment of liver functional reserve, and strategies to expand surgical candidacy; liver transplantation, addressing selection criteria, expanded eligibility concepts, donor source considerations, and the role of bridging and downstaging therapies; and locoregional therapies, encompassing ablative and intra-arterial treatments, their indications as definitive, bridging, or alternative strategies, and their integration within multidisciplinary care pathways. This multidisciplinary consensus provides structured, evidence-based guidance on the use of liver resection, liver transplantation, and locoregional therapies in hepatocellular carcinoma management. By addressing key clinical questions about patient selection, therapeutic indications, and integration of curative and locoregional strategies, these recommendations aim to support consistent, informed decision-making in daily clinical practice and to optimize outcomes for patients eligible for potentially curative treatment.
items.journal: Arquivos brasileiros de cirurgia digestiva : ABCD = Brazilian archives of digestive surgery
authors: Ilka de Fátima Santana Ferreira Boin

items.title: Optimized Activatable Fluorescent and Photoacoustic Imaging Platform toward Precision Detection of Multi-stage Liver Disease.
items.abstract: Molecular imaging utilizing near-infrared (NIR) window and photoacoustic (PA) imaging-which offers high sensitivity, resolution, and tissue penetration-represents a promising approach for visualizing liver diseases. However, there are rare probes for detecting multi-stage liver diseases with high sensitivity, precision, and multi-mode functionality. To address this, we present a novel "Electron Delocalization Equalization" strategy by expanding molecular conjugated system in synergy with charge neutralization to achieve a high-performance NIR/PA molecular platform N5. As a proof of concept, a "single key & dual-locked" probe named N5O was prepared. The NIR and PA signals of N5O are specifically activated by peroxynitrite (ONOO-), which serves as a universal hallmark in the microenvironments of various liver diseases. The design enables rapid response, high sensitivity, and exceptional specificity for imaging multi-stage liver conditions. The strong NIR emission allows accurate assessment of early acute liver injury and diabetic liver disease and reveals that combining hypoglycemic and antioxidant treatments can effectively reverse pathological liver conditions at intermediate stages. In liver cancer models, N5O achieves high-contrast imaging (T/N ∼ 10.7) and accurately outlines tumor margins during fluorescence/PA-guided surgery, substantially lowering postoperative recurrence. Importantly, it also sharply distinguishes human carcinoma from adjacent normal tissue (T/N ∼ 28.1), highlighting its clinical potential.
